summary.headline: NAM India's Q2 FY27 operating profit hit a record INR 5.23 bn (+25% YoY), but PAT fell to INR 3.24 bn after a INR 96.76 crore SEBI settlement charge.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR 7.96 bn and operating profit rose 25% YoY to a record INR 5.23 bn, with operating expenses up 14% YoY. PAT declined both YoY and QoQ to INR 3.24 bn because of a one-time exceptional item: the INR 96.76 crore settlement with SEBI over the Yes Bank AT-1 bond investments by certain NIMF schemes. Mutual fund market share was 9.02%, flat QoQ, and equity yield compressed to 52 bps (ex-arbitrage) from about 54 bps in Q1, which management attributed to telescopic pricing and equity inflows. The Board declared an interim dividend of INR 9.50 per share.

financial_highlights.change: Down YoY and QoQ; hit by exceptional item
INR 89.08 cr management fee reversal incl. interest; INR 7.68 cr regulatory costs

segments.name: Mutual Fund (onshore)
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR 7.87 trillion, up 19.9% YoY and 4.7% QoQ; market share 9.02% (+51 bps YoY, flat QoQ); equity market share 7.40% (+27 bps YoY, +2 bps QoQ).

segments.name: ETF
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2.49 trillion with 21.12% market share, up 135 bps YoY; about 45% share of industry ETF folios and volumes. Gold and silver ETFs at about INR 882 bn, up 6.6% QoQ.

segments.name: Systematic book (SIP/STP)
segments.commentary: Sep-2026 monthly systematic book INR 37 bn, up 2% YoY; annualised INR 445 bn. Excluding STP, SIP book grew 9% YoY. SIP market share 9.84% in Sep-2026.

segments.name: AIF (Nippon India AIF)
segments.commentary: Cumulative commitments INR 99.8 bn, up 14% YoY; INR 4.0 bn raised in Q2. NICO 2 is 55% drawn down after third capital call. Fundraising under way for Listed Equity, Private Credit and Direct VC funds.

segments.name: Offshore and GIFT City
segments.commentary: Offshore managed AUM INR 135 bn; GIFT City AUM USD 45 mn. Management attributed the decline to rupee depreciation and lower FPI flows.

guidance_outlook: Overall cost growth guided at 18% to 20% over the next 6 to 8 quarters, reiterated on the call.
Employee cost expected broadly flat for the MF AMC, with incremental cost mainly in the AIF subsidiary over the next 3 to 6 quarters as senior hires are added.
ESOP expense for FY27 expected at about INR 58 crore; H1 ESOP expense about INR 28 crore.
Management said it will keep investing in technology, brand, digital and people, while staying mindful of the market environment.
SIF launch awaits SEBI clearance; management said it will launch two SIF strategies once approved.
Equity yield expected to keep compressing as equity AUM grows and telescopic pricing applies; no further regulatory impact was expected in Q2 because it occurred in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did equity yield fall QoQ when peers saw yield improvement from mix shift, and was the drop sharp after adjusting for an extra day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the compression to rapid equity AUM growth (among the highest in the industry) and telescopic pricing, with no regulatory impact in Q2 since changes occurred in Q1. Equity yield was 52 bps ex-arbitrage versus about 54 bps in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What was the AT-1 bond case about and what triggered the provision this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the INR 96.76 crore settlement details and said there is nothing further to add until SEBI communicates further. The provision was made after SEBI's in-principle acceptance of the settlement terms during the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company launch SIFs and when?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is awaiting SEBI clearance for SIFs; it has worked on strategy for about a year and plans to launch two SIF strategies once cleared.

qa_highlights.question: How are flows in small-cap and flexi-cap holding up amid corrections, and what is the distributor communication?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it stopped lump-sum flows into its small-cap fund three years ago, and inflows are dispersed to multi-cap and large-cap. Monthly SIP inflows of about INR 32 bn (roughly INR 3,200 crore) are cited as a protection, and distributors are being pushed toward hybrid, multi-asset and fixed-income products.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost and opex outlook, and ESOP expense for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost for the MF AMC should be broadly flat, with incremental cost in AIF over 3 to 6 quarters. Overall cost growth guidance of 18% to 20% over 6 to 8 quarters was maintained; FY27 ESOP expense is about INR 58 crore and H1 about INR 28 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did unique investor count and folios decline QoQ, and is there a direct vs regular trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry investor flows have slowed and NIMF avoids NFO-led acquisition, though SIP folios and total investor accretion remain positive. Direct vs regular mix shifts were called temporary, driven by HNI exits during volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Is the offshore AUM decline reversible and what new offshore products are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to rupee depreciation and lower FPI flows, and said recovery depends on global macro. Offshore plans include feeders into master funds in India via GIFT City, and a possible outbound fund with a strategic partner, still at formative stage.

capex_capacity: No capex or capacity-expansion figures were discussed; the call covered AMC cost plans rather than physical capex.
AIF subsidiary is the expansion area: management expects incremental cost there over the next 3 to 6 quarters as senior hires are added, while the MF AMC cost base stays broadly flat.
NICO 2 (Nippon India Credit Opportunities Fund) is 55% drawn down after the third capital call in Q2 FY27.
Fundraising is under way for the Listed Equity Fund, Private Credit Fund and Direct VC Fund; Q2 AIF commitments were INR 4.0 bn and cumulative commitments INR 99.8 bn.
SIF launch is pending SEBI clearance; management said it has been working on the launch strategy and plans two SIF strategies once cleared.
demand_pricing: Industry QAAUM rose 13% YoY and 5% QoQ to INR 87.2 trillion; industry equity net inflow (ex index and arbitrage) was INR 1.08 trillion, down 5% QoQ.
NIMF QAAUM INR 7.87 trillion, up 19.9% YoY and 4.7% QoQ; MF market share 9.02%, flat QoQ; equity market share 7.40%, up 2 bps QoQ.
Management said equity net sales share is in the high-single digits (about 10%) and SIP market share was 9.84% in Sep-2026.
Equity yield 52 bps ex-arbitrage vs about 54 bps in Q1; debt 25 bps, liquid 12 bps, ETF 25 bps, blended 37 bps. Compression attributed to telescopic pricing and equity AUM growth.

Unique investors 24.3 mn; folios crossed 40 mn, about 2.4 crore unique investors (~38% of industry) per management; NFO-led investor adds were deliberately avoided, and no NFOs were launched in the last two quarters.
ETF AUM INR 2.49 trillion at 21.12% share (+135 bps YoY); gold and silver ETFs about INR 882 bn, up 6.6% QoQ.
Offshore managed AUM INR 135 bn and GIFT City AUM USD 45 mn; management blamed rupee depreciation and lower FPI flows.
risks_watch: Equity yield compression (52 bps ex-arbitrage, down from about 54 bps) as equity AUM grows and telescopic pricing applies; management expects continued compression.
Investor count and folio growth flattened QoQ with no NFOs for two quarters; management says it is not a major concern but it bears watching.
Equity flow sensitivity: HNI exits from large-cap and possible higher redemptions in small-cap and flexi-cap if the market falls further.
AT-1 settlement: further SEBI communication is awaited after the INR 96.76 crore payment, and management declined to elaborate on the alleged non-compliance.
SIF launch timing depends on SEBI clearance; offshore AUM recovery depends on rupee and FPI flows.
key_quotes: Our market share stood at 9.02%, relatively flat QoQ.
The compression in yield was mainly on account of the increase in the equity AUM and due to telescopic pricing.
Any changes due to regulatory change has already happened in the first quarter, so there is nothing on that in this quarter.
summary.management_tone: "Confident on share, SIP and ETF franchise metrics and firm on the cost guidance, but evasive on the AT-1 case (no detail on the alleged non-compliance) and noticeably cautious on industry flows and investor count momentum."

adds.what: No physical capacity additions discussed; AIF subsidiary cost expansion (senior hires) over next 3-6 quarters, not physical capacity

growth.why: No revenue growth guidance given; only opex growth guided at 18-20% over 6-8 quarters (held), with Q2 revenue +21% YoY and operating profit +25% YoY, backed by MF AUM growth (+19.9% YoY), ETF share gains and AIF fundraising, but no physical capacity or order-book figures.
